evidence: Quick Design-only privacy/compliance review. The Design minimizes persisted telemetry, excludes prompts/transcripts/source and personal-content fields, keeps detailed session data private, and limits repository exports to redacted aggregates. One retention/deletion mechanism is inconsistent with the Product boundary and remains prose-only.

findings.issue: Detailed per-session telemetry is declared deleted or irreversibly minimized after terminal commit, although Product requires retention until AC7 reconciliation completes; the Design also names no idempotent cleanup mechanism, completion receipt, or accountable owner.
findings.why: Session-level telemetry can be linkable operational metadata. Deleting it before reconciliation can impair recovery, while a prose-only cleanup promise does not prove bounded retention or deletion of the private copy.
findings.suggestion: Make successful reconciliation of all eight terminal surfaces the cleanup trigger; assign the native-budget or terminal-truth owner; define an idempotent purge/irreversible-minimization operation and receipt; preserve data on cleanup failure; and add a selector proving private session detail is absent after that receipt while only redacted aggregates remain in exports.
